slides.headline: Twenty one soldiers held a fort against thousands - and won a place in history by losing.
The Battle of Saragarhi
slides.body: On the Samana Ridge of the North-West Frontier, a garrison of 21 Sikh soldiers from the 36th Sikhs, led by Havildar Ishar Singh, faced a tribal force numbering in the thousands - vastly outnumbered, with no realistic hope of reinforcement in time.

slides.headline: Every single one fought to the end rather than surrender.
slides.body: All 21 soldiers died holding the post - buying critical time for two nearby forts to prepare their defenses. The British Parliament held a rare standing tribute in their honor, and all 21 were posthumously awarded the Indian Order of Merit, the era's highest gallantry honor open to Indian soldiers.

slides.eyebrow: Why it matters for Viksit Bharat 2047
slides.headline: The Indian Army still marks this day, every year.
slides.body: September 12th is observed as Saragarhi Day - a Regimental Battle Honours Day for the Sikh Regiment, and a state holiday in Punjab since 2017. Nearly 130 years later, the standard it set for holding a position against impossible odds is still the one referenced.
